newsitem.title: USA: US stocks seen steady to higher, much data looms.
newsitem.headline: US stocks seen steady to higher, much data looms.

text.p: A firm U.S. Treasury market and a stronger dollar are expected to lend strength to stocks at Monday's open, but the day's outlook may hinge on release of the first figures in an unusually heavy week-long calendar of economic data.

Pro-dollar comments at the weekend meeting of the Group of Seven countries in Washington helped trigger a sharp dollar rally in Europe. Treasuries also opened firmer ahead of the release of income and spending reports in the U.S.
"I expect the strong dollar and steady bond market to translate into higher prices for stocks," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.

The first economic report due today is a report on U.S. personal income and spending for the month of August, due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT. At 1000 EDT/1400 GMT, the September Chicago Puchasing Managers index (PMI) and U.S. new home saes data for August are both due.
"The Chicago PMI index is often very quirky and I think it will pull back this month," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst at Prudential Securities.

Economists forecast a dip in the Chicago PMI to 56.0 from a surprisingly high 60.0 in August. Personal income is expected to rise 0.6 percent versus 0.1 percent in July and consumption is seen up 0.5 percent versus 0.2 percent.
New home sales are expected to decline to an annualized 744,000 from 783,000 in July.
The data also will hit the market during a day that should see some last-minute scurrying by portfolio managers.
"This is the last day of September, so we'll probably see some window-dressing out there today," said Wachtel.

Surprising strength in the economic reports could undermine the feeling that the Federal Reserve acted correctly in holding interest rates steady at its policy meeting last week, but an indication the economy's growth rate is tapering would reassure markets, analysts said.
"If the news comes in on the weak side, we would probably see interest rates come down to about 6.75 percent before Friday," said Cardillo.
In Tokyo, stocks closed barely higher, with the Nikkei-225 average up nine points to 21,556.
In London, U.S. stocks were mixed, with Microsoft Corp off 2-3/8 to 132 after its warning last Friday that profit margins may decline in 1997. The FTSE-100 eased six points to 3940.4.
The dollar was higher in Tokyo and in Europe, climbing well above the 111 yen level and nearly brushing up against 1.53 German marks.
U.S. Treasuries were firm at the open. The benchmark 30-year bond rose 6/32 to yield 6.89 percent.
The S&P 500 index future edged down 0.4 to 691.0.

Shares in International Business Machines Corp have surged of late and may yet move higher, states the New York Times Marketplace column. The column was cited in Europe for pushing IBM shares slightly higher.
Microsoft Corp shares have rallied sharply as investors shook off worries about the threat from Netscape Communications Corp, the Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column reports.
